stories.notes: Acceptance criteria are empty and this is a complex multi-platform live preview feature requiring real-time content rendering. Openspec needed to elaborate ACs and technical depth; speckit needed to harden testability, security (iframe sandboxing, XSS, content injection), and edge cases. No dependencies or existing spec — blank slate, both agents add value in sequence.

agentContributions.notes: Live Preview is a novel capability — no existing preview integration found. The single attachment point is useContent, which funnels all 236+ component content fetches through getContentByKey. Plugging Live Preview into this hook propagates updates to every consumer automatically. VCs derived solely from description since ACs are empty; they stop at our side of the Contentstack boundary.

Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria, so all 15 criteria are new. I derived them from the story title (Live Preview of Content in CMS), the three-site scope (GO, UP, MX), and the architectural insight that useContent/getContentByKey is the single funnel. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-2 establish the detection/fallback split — preview is opt-in and zero-impact when inactive. (2) AC-3/AC-4/AC-5 cover the core update propagation through useContent, including the no-consumer edge case. (3) AC-6 addresses rapid-update debouncing/throttling as an observable outcome. (4) AC-7/AC-8 cover error handling for malformed payloads and disconnection. (5) AC-9/AC-10 address security — preview data must not leak to non-preview visitors or degrade performance. (6) AC-11 ensures multi-site parity. (7) AC-12 covers client-side navigation preserving preview context. (8) AC-13/AC-14/AC-15 tie the feature to the specific files named in technicalNotes (ContentstackLink, contentCard interface) and ensure backward compatibility of the useContent return contract. CAVEAT: I could not read the actual file contents, so AC-13 through AC-15 are based on file names and paths alone; the exact fields and interfaces may differ. If the implementation details of ContentstackLink or contentCard differ from my assumptions, those criteria should be adjusted accordingly.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value. Openspec identified the architectural insight that useContent/getContentByKey is the single funnel for all component content fetches, making it the natural attachment point for live preview propagation — this is a strong technical elaboration. Speckit then built on that insight to derive 15 verification criteria covering detection/fallback split, update propagation, edge cases (no-consumer, rapid updates), error handling, security (preview data isolation), multi-site parity, navigation context, and backward compatibility of the useContent contract. The agents collaborated in sequence with clear handoff: openspec provided the architectural foundation, speckit hardened it into testable, observable criteria. Speckit's caveat about not reading actual file contents for AC-13 through AC-15 is honest and appropriate — those criteria are tied to ContentstackLink, contentCard interface, and contentstack.ts which all exist per manifest evidence, so the file set is plausible and complete. No missing manifest paths. The empty acceptanceCriteria array is expected per brownfield policy; verification criteria are substantive and testable. No flags needed.
